messages:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — we still need to decide the exact boundary between the Loader API and WeightSource for safetensors + sharded models. do we want the Loader to understand shard manifests or should that be pushed into WeightSource?

stefan: my vote is weight source. loader should be agnostic: open/read/stream bytes. weight source resolves logical shards -> physical files. keeps loader simple and testable.

oz: agree with stef. also: weight source should expose a small async iterator for ranges so we can implement range requests easily (http ranged reads, mmap windows).

sasha: +1. a couple of constraints though: we have a lot of tiny shard files in some experiments and fd limits on GPUs are killing us. weight source should support an aggregated-blob mode (single file with offset index) as well as per-shard mode.

maria: good point on fd limits. do we want the manifest to include both 'file' entries and an optional 'bundle' entry? e.g.

```json
{
  "model_version": "v3",
  "shards": [{"name":"shard-0.safetensors","offset":0,"length":12345}],
  "bundles": [{"path":"shard-bundle-0.dat","map":[{"shard":"shard-0.safetensors","off":0}]}]
}
```

stefan: that's reasonable. manifest should be a minimal contract: list of logical tensors, byte ranges, and optional bundle mapping. weight source implements bundle/unbundle. loader just asks for tensor bytes.

kevin: small ask: make sure the WeightSource exposes metadata for direct mmap when available (fd, offset) so hot paths can mmap() instead of copying. for remote sources we return a fake mmap handle or null.

model-bot: deploy-note: previous hotstart PR assumed loader-level manifest parsing. if we change the boundary we need a small compat shim during rollout.

maria: noted — we should plan a 2-phase rollout: 1) WeightSource supports manifest but Loader still parses (compat), 2) switch parse ownership and remove shim after ~2 weeks.

oz: warmup strategy question: should warmup decisions (priority per tensor/layer) live in the runtime or in the WeightSource? e.g., region server might be able to prioritize early KV cache layers.

sasha: warmup policy should be a contract: WeightSource can accept a priority list and provide a best-effort streaming order. runtime decides priorities (latency-critical layers first). that keeps policies flexible.

stefan: Agree. Implementation detail: make the streaming API accept an ordered list of (tensor_name, priority_hint) and return an async stream of (tensor_name, bytes_chunk). That way weight source can interleave, batch reads, or reorder based on physical locality.

kevin: we also need a synchronous fast-path for very small models where blocking read is cheaper than setting up async streams. maybe WeightSource.read_full(tensor) + WeightSource.stream_chunks(tensor, chunk_size).

maria: good call. add both read_full and stream_chunks to the contract. keep read_full as fallback but runtime should prefer stream when doing large warmups.

oz: another operational tradeoff: many customers upload safetensors archives with inconsistent endianness or vendor-quantized formats. WeightSource should validate tensor headers (dtype, shape, quant params) and expose a standardized descriptor object so loader doesn't have to guess.

sasha: yes please. validation should be optional/expensive-check flag in manifest. by default just basic checksum/shape check; deep dtype verification opt-in for on-prem.

maria: security note: safetensors is good (no code execution) but bundle formats and tarballs can be abused. WeightSource must refuse executing any archive extraction as root; prefer streaming and checksums. add KMS signing verification for private deployments.

stefan: perf note: when shards are small we should coalesce adjacent ranges into single prefetch requests. weight source should implement range coalescing with a tunable window.

kevin: telemetry: expose per-tensor read latency, bytes, source-type (mmap/http/s3), and heap/copy counts so Optimize can recommend bundling or quantization.

maria: agreed. add a lightweight schema for metrics that runtime expects: tensor_name, bytes_read, method, latency_ms.

oz: fallback behavior: if a shard fails to read from primary (e.g., S3) we should have a local tarball cache fallback. weight source should attempt primary -> bundle cache -> remote tarball -> error. plus metrics.

sasha: +1. also a circuit-breaker: if too many partial reads fail, mark the bundle unhealthy and trigger replication/eviction.

stefan: one more compatibility thing: many infra components assume shard filenames end with incremental numbers. we should not require that in manifest. treat names as opaque ids. convert legacy names in the shim.

maria: plan summary:
1) manifest schema v1: logical tensors, ranges, optional bundles, checksum + optional deep-validate flag.
2) WeightSource contract: read_full(tensor), stream_chunks(tensor, chunk_size), stream_prioritized(list[(tensor,priority)]), metadata() including mmap hint and descriptor.
3) Loader: only consume tensor bytes + descriptor, no shard parsing. compatibility shim for 2 weeks.
4) Warmup policy stays in runtime; WeightSource honors priority hints.
5) Telemetry + circuit-breaker + bundle fallback required for rollout.

kevin: looks good. can someone open a tiny RFC doc that lists API prototypes and wire formats? i can help with metrics schema.

maria: i'll draft a short RFC and include examples + shim plan. expect PR tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
